%\VignetteIndexEntry{Filters and Input Builders}
%\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}

```{r, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

The generated Stash operations keep their existing names and arguments. You can continue to pass ordinary nested lists, or use the typed helper functions for common filters.

## Legacy lists remain valid

```r
findScenes(
  scenefilter = list(
    tags = list(value = 182, modifier = "INCLUDES"),
    performers = list(value = 84, modifier = "INCLUDES_ALL")
  )
)
```

The helper form creates the same ordinary list:

```r
findScenes(
  scenefilter = scene_filter(
    tags = includes(182),
    performers = includes_all(84)
  )
)
```

The helpers do not create a new runtime object. They make the shape easier to read and validate field names before a request is sent.

## Common criterion helpers

```r
equals("4k")
includes(182)
includes_all(c(84, 85))
is_null()
not_null()
not_equals("4k")
between(1, 10)
```

These return lists with `value` and `modifier` fields, so they can be composed inside any compatible filter:

```r
tag_filter(name = equals("4k"))
performer_filter(tags = includes(182))
gallery_filter(title = equals("Album"))
group_filter(tags = includes(182))
marker_filter(tags = includes(182))
```

## Hierarchy depth and exclusions

Hierarchical criteria keep the server-side `depth` and `excludes` controls from
the GraphQL schema. A depth of `-1` means unlimited traversal, matching the
legacy nested-list calls:

```r
scene_filter(
  tags = includes(182, depth = -1, excludes = c(183, 184))
)

scene_filter(tags = excludes(182, depth = -1))
```

These values are sent as fields of the criterion input. They do not change the
client-side fragment depth or recursively alter the generated selection set.

## Pagination and search

Use `find_filter()` for common pagination and search fields:

```r
findScenes(
  scenefilter = scene_filter(tags = includes(182)),
  filter = find_filter(per_page = 250, page = 2)
)

findPerformers(filter = find_filter(q = "Leah", per_page = -1))
```

## Resolution and Stash IDs

Resolution is an enum criterion. The value must use a schema enum such as
`FULL_HD`, `FOUR_K`, or `R360P`:

```r
findImages(
  imagefilter = image_filter(
    resolution = greater_than("FULL_HD")
  )
)
```

Stash IDs are endpoint-specific. The endpoint and ID are sent together:

```r
findStudios(
  studiofilter = studio_filter(
    stash_id = stash_id("https://stashdb.org", "abc123")
  )
)
```

The `stash_id` argument is a compatibility alias in `studio_filter()` and is
translated to the schema field `stash_id_endpoint`.

## Strict field checking

The curated helpers reject unknown fields by default:

```r
scene_filter(not_a_schema_field = 1)
#> Error: unknown fields for SceneFilterType: not_a_schema_field
```

For schema additions that are not covered by a curated helper yet, the existing raw-list form remains available. Helper validation can also be disabled deliberately with `.strict = FALSE`.

## Selecting response fields

Generated operations continue to support `.field`:

```r
findTags(
  tagfilter = tag_filter(name = equals("4k")),
  .field = "count"
)
```

The helper layer only constructs variables. Connection setup, GraphQL execution, pagination, and response extraction remain the responsibility of the existing operation functions.
